acceptanceCriteria: Spec requirements in corvint-tasks-attempt-runner-v0 for active delivery, hard-stop salvage, and the context-exhausted repeat state with a configurable count, including per-host support and UNKNOWN when delivery is unsupported

Tests: a worker that never calls a dispatcher verb receives the warn and handoff notices through the delivery path (fake host); a hard-stopped attempt's salvaged note can be read by the next attempt; N consecutive hard stops of one role on one ticket raise the alert and state, and N-1 do not
Build log records the host mechanisms used, limits, and a NOT_RUN live qualification, cross-referenced to V1-1563
body: GitHub issue #1109, follow-up to #1007 (V1-1549). Context thresholds are exposed only passively, through a level file and notices on dispatcher verb output, so review-type workers that only read files never see warnTokens or handoffTokens. Observed: 6 consecutive sessions of one review role on two tickets in about 90 minutes hard-stopped with no verdict, each relaunch re-read the same inputs, and the last session's concrete findings were discarded. Requested: (1) active delivery of warn and handoff notices into the session through the host message or hook mechanism (for example a pre-tool hook or user-turn injection), so the notice arrives on the next turn whatever tool the worker calls; (2) at hardTokens, salvage the last assistant message(s) and any files under the attempt's evidence path into a handoff note on the attempt, readable by the next attempt; (3) after N consecutive hard stops (configurable) of one role on one ticket, report a distinct context-exhausted state with an alert instead of a plain no-progress run. Hosts without a delivery mechanism must report delivery as UNKNOWN/unsupported, never claim it. Related: V1-1563 (live qualification of the estimate and hard stop).
title: dispatch: deliver context warnings into the session, salvage output at the hard stop, alert on repeated hard stops (#1109)
